label: rehearsal
domain_description: Phase transitions, thermodynamics, field theory, non-equilibrium phenomena, renormalization group and scaling, integrable models, turbulence

design.what_is_tested: The central claim under test is that a single declared coarse-graining map, applied to numerically generated configurations of lattice statistical-mechanical models and to numerically integrated driven field equations, predicts the measurable scaling and thermodynamic structure of those systems from the map alone. Concretely: for each system in a fixed, pre-registered battery, we declare in advance (i) a symmetry group and order-parameter dimension, (ii) a spatial dimension, (iii) a conservation-law list, and (iv) a blocking rule with a fixed block factor b. From these declarations, and nothing else, the study emits a numerical prediction for a set of exponents, ratios, and flux laws BEFORE any simulation is run. The study is a falsification test of the proposition that these declared components exhaust what is needed: if two systems that agree in all declared components disagree in a measured exponent beyond the pre-fixed tolerance, the proposition is falsified for that pair; if a system whose declared components are deliberately altered fails to move its measured exponent by the predicted amount, the proposition is falsified for that alteration. The study is deliberately constructed so that a designed-in perturbation (a long-range coupling with tunable decay, an added conservation law, a broken integrability, or a modified forcing band) must produce a specific quantitative shift, and the absence of that shift counts against the design as strongly as an unexpected shift does. Nothing about the outcome is settled by the setup: every predicted number is a real function of the measured configurations, and the estimators are pre-registered as unbiased-in-the-null sense, meaning the null value is not enforced by any normalization, subtraction, or fit constraint in the pipeline.
quantities_measured: Correlation-length exponent nu, estimated from the finite-size scaling collapse of the Binder cumulant crossing locations across at least five linear sizes L in a pre-declared geometric ladder, using the pre-registered two-parameter fit form and no correction-to-scaling term unless declared per-item.
Order-parameter exponent ratio beta/nu, from the size dependence of the mean absolute order parameter at the estimated critical coupling, over the same L ladder.
Susceptibility exponent ratio gamma/nu, from the size dependence of the order-parameter variance times volume at the estimated critical coupling.

Anomalous dimension eta, obtained independently from the equal-time two-point function at fixed separation r = L/4 and separately from gamma/nu via the declared scaling relation, so that the two routes furnish a consistency observable rather than a single number.
Binder cumulant U4 = 1 - <m^4>/(3<m^2>^2) evaluated at the crossing, reported as a size-extrapolated universal value.
Dynamic exponent z, from the integrated autocorrelation time of the order parameter at criticality under a pre-declared local update rule, fit as tau ~ L^z over the L ladder.
Specific-heat singularity index alpha, reported through the hyperscaling combination rather than by direct fit, plus the directly fitted peak-height exponent as a separate declared quantity.
Free-energy density difference between two declared boundary conditions at fixed L, used as a probe of the universal amplitude ratio in the finite-size scaling function.
Energy-flux constancy across scales in the driven field system, measured as the third-order structure function or its scale-resolved spectral-transfer analogue over a declared band of wavenumbers.
Spectral slope of the scale-resolved energy density over the same declared inertial band, fit as a power law in wavenumber with the band endpoints fixed before the run.

Intermittency correction spectrum: scaling exponents zeta_p of order-p structure functions for p in a declared finite set, reported with their deviation from the linear-in-p reference implied by pure flux constancy.

Entropy production rate in the driven non-equilibrium steady state, measured as the log-ratio of forward and time-reversed path probabilities over a declared trajectory length, together with the mean housekeeping heat flux, as two routes to the same quantity.

Fluctuation-relation residual: the deviation of the measured log-ratio of positive to negative entropy-production histogram bins from linearity in the entropy production, quantified as the maximum absolute residual over a declared central range of the histogram.
Level-spacing ratio statistic of the spectrum of the declared finite-size quantum or transfer-matrix operator, computed in a fixed symmetry sector, as a scalar summary of spectral correlation.
Number of independent conserved quantities detected numerically as the rank of a declared correlation matrix of candidate local densities, thresholded at a pre-fixed singular-value cutoff.

Ballistic transport coefficient, measured as the long-time saturation of the current autocorrelation integral, normalized by the declared static susceptibility, and reported as a dimensionless Drude-like weight.
Relaxation profile of a declared inhomogeneous initial state, summarized as the position of the front measured at half the asymptotic plateau, fit against time to extract a front-spreading exponent.
Coarsening length scale after a quench, extracted from the first zero-crossing of the equal-time correlation function, fit as a power law in time.
Two-time correlation and response functions after a quench, combined into the fluctuation-dissipation ratio in the aging regime, reported at declared time pairs.

Renormalization-group flow displacement: for each declared blocking step at factor b, the vector of measured couplings in a fixed truncated basis, and the largest eigenvalue of the numerically estimated linearization of the blocking map around its fixed point.
Wall-clock and core-hour cost per measured quantity, logged for every run, as a first-class recorded quantity so that the compute limit is auditable rather than asserted.
controls: Exactly-solved anchor control: a lattice model in the battery for which an independent, pre-registered high-precision reference value of nu and beta/nu is fixed in a sealed file before any run. The pipeline must reproduce these anchor values inside the pre-fixed tolerance. If the anchor fails, no other item in the study may be interpreted, because a pipeline that misses a known number cannot adjudicate an unknown one. The anchor value is declared numerically in the sealed file and is not re-derived from the runs.

Null-coupling control: the same estimator battery applied to a system at a coupling deliberately placed far from any transition, on the disordered side by a declared margin. Every exponent estimator must return a null-consistent result, meaning no power-law fit passes the declared goodness threshold and the correlation length must saturate below a declared fraction of L. An estimator that manufactures a clean exponent here is manufacturing exponents everywhere.

Shuffled-configuration control: configurations with sites randomly permuted within each sample, destroying spatial correlation but preserving all single-site statistics. Correlation-derived quantities (eta, spectral slope, structure-function exponents, coarsening length) must collapse to their declared trivial values. This separates genuine spatial structure from single-point histogram artifacts.

Time-reversal control for the non-equilibrium items: an equilibrium-drive-off run of the same code path, in which the measured entropy production rate must be statistically indistinguishable from zero at the declared precision, and the fluctuation-relation residual must be within the declared band. A pipeline that reports finite entropy production with the drive off has an integration or discretization bias, and its driven numbers are uninterpretable.

Seed-replication control: every reported number is computed from at least four independent seed groups whose group-to-group scatter is compared with the within-group statistical error. If the between-group scatter exceeds the within-group error by more than the declared factor, the error bar is declared underestimated and the number is reported as inconclusive rather than as a measurement.

Discretization control: every field-theoretic and turbulence item is repeated at two declared grid resolutions and two declared time steps in a fixed factorial. Quantities that shift between resolutions by more than the declared fraction of their statistical error are marked resolution-limited and excluded from adjudication, with the exclusion recorded.

Integrability-breaking control: for the integrable-model items, a paired run with a declared integrability-breaking term of strength epsilon, including epsilon = 0 as one arm. Quantities claimed to be diagnostic of integrability must move monotonically with epsilon over the declared epsilon ladder; a flat response falsifies the diagnostic claim.

Estimator-swap control: nu is estimated by two pre-declared, structurally different routes (cumulant-crossing drift and derivative-of-cumulant scaling). The two routes must agree inside the declared tolerance. Disagreement is reported as an estimator-dependence failure and not resolved by choosing the more agreeable route after the fact.

Blind-labelling control: all analysis code is executed on runs whose system-identity labels are replaced by opaque tokens, with the token map held sealed until the full quantity table is frozen. This is enforced by the pipeline refusing to read the map file before the freeze timestamp is written.
bars: Anchor bar: the anchor system's nu must be recovered within 3 percent of the sealed reference value, and beta/nu within 4 percent, each with a statistical error no larger than half the stated tolerance. Failure of either voids interpretation of the whole study.

Universality-collision bar: for any pre-declared pair of systems agreeing in all declared components (symmetry, order-parameter dimension, spatial dimension, conservation list, interaction range class), the measured nu values must agree within a combined tolerance of 4 percent or 2.5 combined standard errors, whichever is larger. A disagreement exceeding both is a positive falsification of the sufficiency proposition for that pair.

Declared-component sensitivity bar: for each declared component that is deliberately altered in a paired run (order-parameter dimension changed by one; spatial dimension changed by one; one conservation law added; interaction range decay exponent moved across the declared threshold), the measured nu must shift by at least 8 percent of its unaltered value and by at least 4 combined standard errors. A shift smaller than both bars means the declared component was not load-bearing, which falsifies the claim that the declared set is the right set.

Scaling-relation bar: the two independent routes to eta (direct two-point fit and the gamma/nu relation) must agree within 0.05 in absolute eta. The hyperscaling combination must close within 0.06 in absolute alpha. These are consistency bars whose failure indicates either a wrong relation or a broken estimator, and the design does not permit choosing between those two after the fact without a declared tie-break run.

Binder-value bar: the size-extrapolated U4 for two systems declared to share a universality class must agree within 0.010 absolute. This is a shape observable independent of any critical-coupling estimate and therefore is not settled by the fitting procedure.

Dynamic-exponent bar: z must be resolved with a statistical error below 0.06, and two systems with the same declared static class but different declared conservation lists must differ in z by at least 0.25. A null difference falsifies the claim that the conservation list controls the dynamic class.

Flux-constancy bar: over the declared inertial band, the measured flux must be constant to within 12 percent peak-to-peak of its band mean, and the band must span at least a factor of 8 in wavenumber. A band that cannot meet the width requirement at the declared resolution is reported as absent, not narrowed to fit.

Spectral-slope bar: the fitted slope over the declared band must have a statistical error below 0.08 and must be stable to within 0.10 when the band endpoints are each moved by a factor of 1.5 inward. Instability beyond that is a failed measurement, not a soft result.

Intermittency bar: the deviation of zeta_p from the linear-in-p reference at the largest declared p must exceed 3 combined standard errors for the claim of a nonlinear exponent spectrum to be recorded, and must exceed 0.15 in absolute exponent for it to be recorded as physically resolved rather than merely statistically detected.

Entropy-production route-agreement bar: the path-ratio route and the housekeeping-flux route must agree within 10 percent of the larger value, with the drive-off control pinned below 2 percent of the smallest driven value measured. Route disagreement beyond that bar falsifies the identification of the two quantities under the declared dynamics.

Fluctuation-relation bar: over the declared central histogram range, the maximum absolute residual from linearity must be below 0.12 in natural-log units, and the fitted slope of the log-ratio against entropy production must lie within 0.08 of unity. A slope outside that window with the drive on, when the drive-off control passes, is a falsification of the declared symmetry for that dynamics.

Conserved-quantity-count bar: the rank estimate must be integer-stable under a factor-of-3 change in the singular-value cutoff and under doubling the trajectory length. A rank that moves under either perturbation is reported as undetermined. For the integrability-breaking ladder, the detected count must decrease by at least one between epsilon = 0 and the largest declared epsilon.

Ballistic-weight bar: the dimensionless Drude-like weight must exceed 0.05 at epsilon = 0 with a statistical error below 0.01, and must fall by at least a factor of 3 at the largest declared epsilon. Failure of either half falsifies the transport diagnostic as declared.

Coarsening-exponent bar: the fitted growth exponent must have a statistical error below 0.03 and must be stable within 0.04 when the fit window start time is doubled. Two systems differing only in the declared conservation list must differ in this exponent by at least 0.10.

RG-eigenvalue bar: the largest eigenvalue of the linearized blocking map, converted to a length exponent through the declared block factor b, must agree with the finite-size-scaling nu within 6 percent. The eigenvalue must additionally be stable within 5 percent when b is changed from its primary declared value to the declared secondary value. Instability under b is a falsification of the truncated-basis blocking as implemented.

Statistical-power bar: every bar above is accompanied by a pre-fixed minimum sample size chosen so that the declared effect size would be detected with probability at least 0.9 at a two-sided significance of 0.01 under the declared noise model. A run that terminates below that sample size is reported as underpowered and its bar is not adjudicated in either direction.

Multiplicity bar: with the item count fixed at fifteen, the family-wise significance threshold is set by a pre-registered Holm correction at family-wise 0.05, and all raw p-values are reported alongside their corrected verdicts. No item's verdict may be read off an uncorrected p-value.
failure_conditions: The anchor control misses its sealed reference value beyond the anchor bar. The entire study is then declared void and no item verdict is reported, because a pipeline that cannot reproduce a fixed known number has no standing to adjudicate unknown ones.

The null-coupling control returns a power-law fit passing the declared goodness threshold, or the shuffled-configuration control returns a non-trivial correlation exponent. Either indicates the estimator invents structure, and all correlation-derived items are voided.
The drive-off time-reversal control returns an entropy production rate above the declared pinning bar. All non-equilibrium items are then voided regardless of how clean their driven numbers look.

Seed-group scatter exceeds within-group error by more than the declared factor for more than one third of reported quantities. The error model is then declared wrong and the study reports only the error-model failure.
The estimator-swap control shows the two nu routes disagreeing beyond tolerance for the anchor system. This is a pipeline failure rather than a physics result and voids all exponent items.

Every declared-component alteration produces a shift below the sensitivity bar. This would mean the declared components are not the ones that matter, which is a falsification of the design's core proposition, and it must be reported as such rather than reinterpreted as a universality finding.

Conversely, systems agreeing in every declared component disagree beyond the collision bar in more than one declared pair. This falsifies the sufficiency of the declared component list and the design is judged to have failed at its stated purpose.

The inertial band cannot be established at the declared minimum width of a factor of 8 at either declared resolution. The turbulence items are then reported as not measurable at the available compute, and no slope or intermittency number is reported at reduced band width.
The RG blocking eigenvalue fails its b-stability bar. The blocking-derived items are voided and the finite-size-scaling items are reported separately without the cross-check.

Any analysis choice not present in this preregistration is found in the executed code path, as detected by a diff of the frozen analysis module against the executed module. The affected items are voided.
The blind-label seal is broken before the quantity table is frozen, as detected by the pipeline's access log. All items whose numbers were computed after the break are voided.
More than four of the fifteen items terminate underpowered. The study is then reported as an aborted design, with the compute estimate declared wrong, rather than as a partial result set.
forbidden_inputs: Any published or tabulated numerical value of any exponent, amplitude ratio, universal cumulant value, spectral slope, or intermittency exponent for any system in the battery, other than the single anchor reference sealed before the run and used only for the anchor control.

Any exact analytic solution, closed-form partition function, Bethe-ansatz result, conformal-field-theory operator dimension, or exactly known transfer-matrix spectrum for any battery system other than the anchor, whether entered as a fit constraint, an initial guess, a prior, or a plausibility filter on the output.

Any correction-to-scaling term, effective-exponent drift term, or additional fit parameter introduced after seeing the data. The fit forms are frozen per item, and adding a parameter is permitted only by declaring a new item in a subsequent, separately preregistered study.

Any choice of critical coupling taken from outside the run. The critical coupling must be estimated from the same runs by the declared crossing procedure, and no external value may seed, bound, or shift the fit.

Any post-hoc adjustment to the inertial band endpoints, the fit window start times, the histogram central range, the singular-value cutoff, the L ladder, or the epsilon ladder. These are all frozen numbers.

Any dropping of an L value, a seed group, a resolution arm, or an epsilon arm on grounds other than the pre-declared outlier rule, which is itself stated as a fixed numeric criterion applied identically to controls and to test items.
Any machine-learned or fitted surrogate for a measured quantity. Every reported number is computed by the declared estimator on the raw configurations or trajectories.
Any tuning of the coarse-graining map, the truncated coupling basis, the block factor, or the update rule after inspecting any measured exponent.
Any use of the label map or system identities inside any estimator, so that the estimator cannot condition on what system it is looking at.

Any expectation, hypothesis, or prior about which universality classes the battery systems belong to, entered as a grouping in the analysis. Groupings are defined solely by the declared components, which are fixed before the run and recorded in the sealed file.
design.stopping_rules: Stopping is time-and-sample based, never result based. Each item has a pre-fixed target sample size N_target set by its statistical-power bar, and a pre-fixed core-hour allocation. An item stops when N_target is reached, at which point its numbers are frozen and no further samples may be added, or when its allocation is exhausted, at which point it is reported as underpowered and its bar is not adjudicated. Interim looks at any item's estimated value are prohibited; the only permitted interim monitoring is of sample count, wall-clock, thermal state, and control-passage, and the control-passage check is limited to the anchor, null-coupling, shuffled, and drive-off controls, each of which is evaluated once at 20 percent of allocation. If any of those four controls fails at the 20 percent check, the study halts immediately and reports a pipeline failure without proceeding to test items, which saves the remaining 80 percent of compute. There is no adaptive reallocation between items after the start, and no extension of any allocation for any reason including a near-miss on a bar. Total compute limit for the entire study is fixed at 6000 GPU-hours plus 40000 CPU-core-hours, apportioned before the run as: 30 percent to the lattice critical-scaling items, 30 percent to the driven-field and turbulence items, 20 percent to the integrable and transport items, 15 percent to the non-equilibrium entropy-production and aging items, and 5 percent reserved for the controls, with the control reserve spent first. Nothing may draw on another item's share. The freeze timestamp for the full quantity table is written before the label map is opened, and the study ends at that timestamp regardless of which bars were met.

items.statement: The declared symmetry group and order-parameter dimension, together with spatial dimension and conservation list, are sufficient to fix the correlation-length exponent nu, so that two battery systems agreeing in all four declared components share nu.
items.quantitative_test: For each of the three pre-declared same-component pairs, estimate nu on both members from Binder-cumulant crossing drift across the frozen L ladder (five sizes, geometric factor 1.5), with the second, structurally different derivative-of-cumulant route computed in parallel. Compare the two members' nu values using a combined-standard-error statistic on blinded labels.
items.bars: Agreement within 4 percent relative or 2.5 combined standard errors, whichever is larger. Each member's nu must carry a statistical error below 2 percent. The two estimator routes must agree within 3 percent on each member before the pair comparison is read.
items.falsifier: Any declared pair whose nu values differ by more than both the 4 percent and the 2.5-sigma bar, while both members pass the estimator-swap and seed-scatter controls, falsifies the sufficiency of the declared component list. Because the two members are simulated by different microscopic rules and are only asserted to match through the declared components, nothing in the setup forces their exponents to coincide.

items.statement: Changing the declared order-parameter dimension by one, holding all other declared components fixed, moves nu by a resolvable amount.
items.quantitative_test: Run the paired battery at order-parameter dimensions n and n+1 in the same spatial dimension, same lattice, same update rule, same L ladder, same sample size. Compute delta_nu as the relative change and its combined standard error.
items.bars: delta_nu must exceed 8 percent of the n-value and 4 combined standard errors. Statistical error on each nu below 2 percent.
items.falsifier: A measured shift below both bars falsifies the claim that order-parameter dimension is a load-bearing declared component. This outcome is not excluded by the setup: the two runs share every line of simulation code except the component-count constant, so a null shift is a physically possible and reportable result.

items.statement: The two independent routes to the anomalous dimension eta, namely a direct fit of the equal-time two-point function at separation L/4 and the value implied by the measured gamma/nu through the declared scaling relation, agree.
items.quantitative_test: On each battery system, compute eta_direct from the L-dependence of the two-point function at fixed r/L = 1/4, and eta_relation from the measured gamma/nu. Report the signed difference and its combined error.
items.bars: Absolute difference below 0.05, with each route's statistical error below 0.02. The shuffled-configuration control must return eta_direct at its declared trivial value within 0.03.
items.falsifier: A signed difference exceeding 0.05 on a system whose controls all pass falsifies the joint validity of the declared scaling relation and the two estimators as implemented. The setup does not enforce agreement because the two routes use disjoint moments of the configuration ensemble: one uses a distance-resolved correlator, the other a volume-integrated variance.

items.statement: The size-extrapolated Binder cumulant value U4 is a shape observable of the declared universality class and is therefore equal across the declared same-component pairs, independently of any critical-coupling estimate.
items.quantitative_test: Extrapolate U4 at the crossing to infinite L with the frozen two-term extrapolation form, on both members of each declared pair, on blinded labels. Compare absolute values.
items.bars: Pairwise agreement within 0.010 absolute, with extrapolation uncertainty below 0.004 on each member. The null-coupling control must return U4 at its declared disordered value within 0.02.
items.falsifier: A pairwise U4 difference above 0.010 with both members passing controls falsifies the class assignment implied by the declared components, and does so independently of item I1 because U4 does not depend on locating the critical coupling to the same precision that nu does.

items.statement: The declared conservation list, and not the declared static symmetry, controls the dynamic exponent z.
items.quantitative_test: Take two systems with identical declared static components but different declared conservation lists, one with a locally conserved order parameter and one without, under the declared local update rule. Measure z from the L-scaling of the integrated order-parameter autocorrelation time at the estimated critical coupling.
items.bars: Each z resolved with statistical error below 0.06. The two z values must differ by at least 0.25. Additionally, the two systems' nu values must agree within 4 percent, confirming the static class is genuinely shared, or the item is reported as inconclusive rather than adjudicated.
items.falsifier: A z difference below 0.25 while the statics match falsifies the claim that the conservation list controls the dynamic class. A z difference above 0.25 accompanied by a nu difference above 4 percent falsifies the premise that the pair shares a static class and voids the item, which is a distinct and pre-declared outcome.

items.statement: Moving the declared interaction-range decay exponent across a pre-declared threshold value changes nu, and holding it on one side of the threshold leaves nu unchanged as the decay exponent varies within that side.
items.quantitative_test: Run a ladder of four long-range decay exponents, two on each side of the declared threshold, at fixed symmetry, order-parameter dimension, spatial dimension, and conservation list. Measure nu at each rung. Compute the within-side spread and the across-threshold jump.
items.bars: Across-threshold change in nu at least 8 percent and 4 combined standard errors. Within-side spread below 4 percent and below 2.5 combined standard errors on each side. Statistical error on each nu below 2 percent.
items.falsifier: Either a within-side spread exceeding its bar, or an across-threshold jump below its bar, falsifies the declared threshold as the correct dividing line for the range component. Both directions are live because the decay exponent enters the simulation as a continuous parameter with no discontinuity built into the code.

items.statement: In the driven field system, the energy flux is constant across a declared band of wavenumbers spanning at least a factor of 8, and the spectral energy density over that same band follows a single power law.
items.quantitative_test: In the statistically stationary driven state, compute the scale-resolved flux and the spectral energy density over the frozen band. Measure peak-to-peak flux variation as a fraction of the band mean, and fit the spectral slope with the frozen band endpoints. Repeat at both declared resolutions and both declared time steps.
items.bars: Flux constancy within 12 percent peak-to-peak. Band width at least a factor of 8. Spectral-slope statistical error below 0.08 and slope stable within 0.10 when each endpoint moves inward by a factor of 1.5. Resolution-to-resolution slope shift below 0.10 or the item is marked resolution-limited.
items.falsifier: Flux variation above 12 percent over a band that meets the width requirement, or a slope that moves more than 0.10 under the declared endpoint perturbation, falsifies the joint claim of flux constancy and single-power-law scaling at the achieved resolution. The design forbids narrowing the band to rescue either, so the failure cannot be absorbed.

items.statement: The scaling exponents zeta_p of order-p structure functions in the driven field system deviate from the linear-in-p reference implied by pure flux constancy, and the deviation grows with p.
items.quantitative_test: Over the same frozen band as I7, fit zeta_p for the declared set of orders p. Compute the deviation from the linear reference anchored at the declared low order, and test monotonic growth of the deviation across the p set.
items.bars: At the largest declared p, deviation must exceed 3 combined standard errors and 0.15 in absolute exponent for a positive record. Monotonic growth must hold across the p set with no reversal exceeding 1 combined standard error. Convergence of the p-th moment must be certified by the declared tail-fraction criterion or the order is dropped by rule, with the drop recorded.
items.falsifier: Deviations at all p inside 3 sigma and 0.15, with I7's band established and its controls passed, falsifies the nonlinearity claim. A non-monotonic deviation exceeding the reversal bar falsifies the growth claim separately. Neither is settled by the setup because the fits are unconstrained across p.

items.statement: The steady-state entropy production rate measured by the path-probability-ratio route equals the rate measured by the housekeeping-heat-flux route, and both vanish when the drive is switched off.
items.quantitative_test: In the declared driven non-equilibrium steady state, compute the log-ratio of forward to time-reversed path probabilities over the frozen trajectory length, and independently accumulate the housekeeping heat flux. Repeat the same code path with the drive amplitude set to zero.
items.bars: Route agreement within 10 percent of the larger value, each with statistical error below 4 percent. Drive-off rate pinned below 2 percent of the smallest driven rate measured. Both routes measured at both declared time steps with shift below their statistical error.
items.falsifier: Route disagreement above 10 percent with the drive-off control passing falsifies the identification of the two quantities under the declared discretized dynamics. A drive-off rate above the pinning bar falsifies the integrator as entropy-neutral and voids all non-equilibrium items, a pre-declared and distinct failure.

items.statement: The steady-state entropy-production distribution satisfies a linear log-ratio symmetry with unit slope over the declared central range.
items.quantitative_test: Histogram the trajectory-resolved entropy production over the frozen trajectory length, form the log-ratio of the positive and negative bins, and fit it against entropy production over the frozen central range. Record the fitted slope and the maximum absolute residual from linearity.
items.bars: Fitted slope within 0.08 of unity. Maximum absolute residual below 0.12 in natural-log units. At least the declared minimum count in the least-populated bin of the central range, or the range is reported as unpopulated and the item as underpowered.
items.falsifier: A fitted slope outside the 0.08 window, or a residual above 0.12, with the drive-off control passing and the bin-count requirement met, falsifies the declared symmetry for this dynamics. Nothing in the histogramming enforces unit slope, since the negative-entropy bins are populated only by rare trajectories the simulation does not steer toward.

items.statement: The number of independent local conserved densities detected in the integrable-model arm decreases as the declared integrability-breaking strength epsilon increases along the frozen epsilon ladder.
items.quantitative_test: At each rung of the frozen epsilon ladder including epsilon = 0, build the declared correlation matrix of candidate local densities from trajectories of the frozen length and take its numerical rank at the frozen singular-value cutoff. Check integer stability under a factor-of-3 cutoff change and under doubled trajectory length.
items.bars: Rank must be integer-stable under both perturbations at every rung, or that rung is reported as undetermined. The rank at the largest declared epsilon must be at least one lower than at epsilon = 0. Rank must be non-increasing along the ladder with no increase of more than zero counts.
items.falsifier: A rank that is unchanged between epsilon = 0 and the largest declared epsilon, while stable under both perturbations, falsifies the rank estimator as a diagnostic of the declared conserved structure. A rank that increases with epsilon falsifies it more strongly. The setup does not fix the count, since the rank is read off measured singular values of trajectory data.

items.statement: The dimensionless ballistic transport weight is finite at epsilon = 0 and is suppressed by integrability breaking.
items.quantitative_test: Measure the long-time saturation of the current autocorrelation integral, normalized by the declared static susceptibility, at each rung of the frozen epsilon ladder. Certify saturation by the declared plateau criterion over the frozen late-time window.
items.bars: Weight at epsilon = 0 above 0.05 with statistical error below 0.01, and plateau criterion satisfied. Weight at the largest declared epsilon at least a factor of 3 lower. Both measured at the two declared system sizes with size-to-size shift below the statistical error, or the item is marked size-limited.
items.falsifier: A weight at epsilon = 0 below 0.05, or a suppression factor under 3 at the largest epsilon, falsifies the transport diagnostic as declared. This is a genuine two-sided risk because the plateau is measured, not imposed, and the normalization by static susceptibility is computed from an independent equal-time average.

items.statement: After the declared quench, the coarsening length grows as a power of time with an exponent set by the declared conservation list, and the two conservation arms differ in that exponent.
items.quantitative_test: Quench both arms, identical except for the declared conservation list, from the declared high-temperature initial condition to the declared final coupling. Extract the coarsening length from the first zero-crossing of the equal-time correlation function and fit its growth exponent over the frozen time window. Repeat with the fit window start time doubled.
items.bars: Exponent statistical error below 0.03. Stability within 0.04 under the doubled window start. Difference between the two conservation arms at least 0.10. Coarsening length must remain below the declared fraction of the box size throughout the fit window or the window is truncated by rule.
items.falsifier: An inter-arm difference below 0.10 while both exponents pass their stability bars falsifies the claim that the conservation list sets the coarsening exponent. Failure of the stability bar in either arm falsifies the power-law form over the declared window and is reported as such rather than as a differing exponent.

items.statement: In the aging regime after the quench, the fluctuation-dissipation ratio formed from the measured two-time correlation and response functions departs from its equilibrium value by a resolvable amount, and that departure is absent in the equilibrated control.
items.quantitative_test: At the frozen set of two-time pairs in the aging regime, measure the two-time correlation and the conjugate response under the declared perturbation protocol, and form their ratio. Run the same protocol on a system equilibrated at the same final coupling for the declared equilibration time.
items.bars: Departure from the equilibrium value at the latest declared time pair must exceed 4 combined standard errors and 0.10 in the ratio. The equilibrated control's ratio must sit within 0.05 of the equilibrium value. Response amplitude must satisfy the declared linearity check at two perturbation strengths differing by a factor of 2, with ratio shift below its statistical error.
items.falsifier: A departure inside both bars in the aging arm, with the linearity check passing and the equilibrated control on value, falsifies the claim of a resolvable aging departure at the declared times. An equilibrated control off value by more than 0.05 falsifies the response protocol itself and voids the item, a separately declared outcome.

items.statement: The correlation-length exponent obtained from the largest eigenvalue of the numerically linearized blocking map, at the declared block factor, agrees with the finite-size-scaling nu, and is stable when the block factor is changed to its declared secondary value.
items.quantitative_test: On the anchor system and on one declared test system, perform the frozen blocking procedure in the frozen truncated coupling basis at the primary block factor b1, estimate the linearization of the map around its numerically located fixed point by finite differences with the frozen step, take the largest eigenvalue, and convert it to a length exponent using b1. Repeat at the declared secondary block factor b2. Compare each to the finite-size-scaling nu of item I1 on the same system.
items.bars: Agreement with finite-size-scaling nu within 6 percent on each system. Stability of the converted exponent within 5 percent between b1 and b2. Eigenvalue estimate stable within 3 percent under a factor-of-2 change in the finite-difference step. Truncated basis frozen and unchanged between b1 and b2.
items.falsifier: A converted exponent differing from the finite-size-scaling nu by more than 6 percent on the anchor system, where the anchor control has already passed, falsifies the blocking implementation in the declared truncated basis. Instability beyond 5 percent between b1 and b2 falsifies the block-factor independence of the map as implemented. Neither follows from the setup, because the eigenvalue comes from finite differences of a map acting on measured coupling estimates and is nowhere constrained to reproduce the crossing-based number.
